page: Microsoft Azure E20s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 10 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 160.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include any local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results place the E20s_v7 in the average performance tier for most standard operations, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2232.95 and a multi-core score of 20536.75. However, it demonstrates strong performance in single-threaded compression tasks, achieving 35.43 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.68 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 364.6 tokens/sec, while medium 7B model generation runs at an average speed of 18.72 tokens/sec. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 1518.31 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 139.09 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the E20s_v7 is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage for persistent data. This configuration offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-speed local scratch space, as users avoid paying for unused local SSD capacity. The high memory density and strong single-threaded performance make this server well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
